## Contract checklist

- [x] `ContextUsage` (C1) — declared here, so wave 2's deletion of `ContextReadout.tsx` orphans nothing
- [x] `ModelOption.priceIn?: number | null` (optional — D1-B fills it; a server without the field still compiles)
- [x] `ModelNote` / `MODEL_INSIGHTS` / `modelNoteFor` — copy client-side, price server-side
- [x] `splitModels(config, current, primaryCount = MODEL_PRIMARY_COUNT)` — current model always primary, matched by exact id then family
- [x] `effortIndex` / `effortAt` — clamped, never −1
- [x] `UsageLimitWire` / `UsageLimitsResponse` — percent + `resetsAt` + optional `scope`, MIRRORED comment naming `src/lib/claude-usage.ts`
- [x] `UsageLimit`, `USAGE_STALE_MS`, `USAGE_MAX_AGE_MS`, `usageLimits(ctx, res, now)` — pure, `now` injected
- [x] `useUsageLimits(enabled)` — `GET /api/agent/usage-limits`, 60 s, `queryKey: ['agent-usage-limits']` with no id so panes share one cache entry and one timer

## Deviations

**One, inside the owned file.** The plan didn't mention it: `modelLabelFor` had the family list `['opus','sonnet','haiku','fable']` inlined, and I needed the identical match for `modelNoteFor` and `splitModels`. Rather than a second and third copy I extracted `modelFamily(id)` and pointed `modelLabelFor` at it — behaviour-identical (the 18 sibling tests confirm), and it means adding a family can't leave a model labelled but undescribed. A test asserts every `MODEL_FAMILIES` member has an insight, so that stays true.

Two judgement calls the plan left open, both documented in the code:
- **Unknown effort level → thumb at index 0**, while the trigger keeps printing `effortLabel(level)`. The position is a guess; the reading stays truthful. Same discipline as `modelLabelFor` never substituting a default for an unrecognised id.
- **`staleAsOf` is non-null only when an account bar survived** — an "as of 09:00" caption under a popover showing nothing but the context bar would be labelling the wrong thing.

Nothing in the plan turned out to be wrong; no scope expanded. `usageLimits` re-validates percent range even though `readUsageLimits` (D1-B) already drops out-of-range values — deliberate defense in depth at the boundary, since a clamped lie renders identically to the truth.
